sentences.text: Albertadromeus was a small, bipedal, herbivorous dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.

The genus name Albertadromeus means "runner from Alberta", referencing its inferred ability to run, while the species name syntarsus means "together-ankle", referring to the fusion of the distal fibula to the distal tibia.

It possessed an elongated tibia that indicates it was adapted for running, a distal fibula reduced to a thin bone sheet fused to the front of the tibia for the distal third of its length, and a prominent cnemial crest on the tibia that projected upward and outward.
The tibia of Albertadromeus is slightly longer than that of Orodromeus and significantly longer than those of Parksosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Hypsilophodon, Dryosaurus, and Stegoceras.
Albertadromeus is the smallest known herbivorous dinosaur in Canada, measuring about 1.6 meters long and weighing 16 kilograms.
Its distal fibula was reduced to a thin bone sheet fused to the front of the tibia for the distal third of its length.

Albertadromeus was described and named by Caleb Marshall Brown, David C. Evans, Michael J. Ryan, and Anthony P. Russell in 2013, and the type specimen is housed in the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology in Drumheller, Alberta.
Albertadromeus was a herbivore that likely specialized in eating ferns and low vegetation.
Albertadromeus lived in an ancient coastal plain environment, and studies suggest the paleoenvironment of the Oldman Formation, where Albertadromeus fossils were found, was an ancient coastal plain.

The Oldman Formation contained fossils of various dinosaurs that shared the same environment with Albertadromeus, including theropods like Saurornitholestes and Daspletosaurus, ceratopsians like Albertaceratops and Chasmosaurus, and hadrosaurids like Brachylophosaurus and Parasaurolophus.
Albertadromeus is classified as a member of the class Ornithischia.
Albertadromeus is classified within the family Thescelosauridae.

Researchers created the subfamily Orodrominae to group species like Albertadromeus that are closely related to Orodromeus, and Albertadromeus belongs to the subfamily Orodrominae, which also includes Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus, and Oryctodromeus.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Albertadromeus is closely related to Zephyrosaurus and Orodromeus.
Albertadromeus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77 to 76 million years ago, and lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
